title: RUBRIC-HIDDEN: did the rubric tests hide a real per-leaf effect, through the pairs they discarded or through pooling? (zero calls)
question: (1) On the NON-decidable pairs every rubric test excluded (1,030 of 1,974 on R3), does a rubric make the judge abstain instead of inventing a winner? (2) A power analysis of the pooled tests against the per-anchor effects observed.

criteria.text: the unmeasured pairs: does a rubric make the judge abstain on non-decidable pairs?
criteria.value: REFUTED: invented-winner rate on non-decidable pairs 62.2% without the card and 63.6% with it on Mistral (grok 62.1 -> 59.5; card + worked neighbours 61.0); the longer answer wins 80-82% in every arm: the rubric buys no abstention, so nothing hid there

LIVE: pooled tests had 944-946 decidable pairs at a discordant rate near 0.05, powering them for ~3pp (1pp would need ~3,900); per anchor only 30-144 pairs, powering each for 10-20pp; the observed per-anchor gains (RUBRIC-512 Philosophy +16.7, Biology +7.4; RK-1b Business +9.1, Chemistry +6.0, History +4.8, Engineering +4.7; Economics -6.2) were never individually testable; leaf-level rubrics were tested ONCE (RUBRIC-512 +1.8pp, p 0.0498) and the clean follow-up LEAF-SS was cancelled by a gate

falsifier.note: what would settle it: ~215 decidable pairs per anchor to detect 6pp; the cheap version on the four anchors where the observed gain exceeded 6pp (~4k calls) was registered as LEAF-POWERED

sentence_of_record: RUBRIC-HIDDEN (2026-09-14, zero calls): mechanism 1 REFUTED: the invented-winner rate on non-decidable pairs is 62.2% without the card and 63.6% with it on Mistral (62.1 -> 59.5 on grok), and the length preference stays near 81% in every arm, so the rubric buys no abstention and nothing hid in the discarded pairs; mechanism 2 LIVE: pooled tests were powered for ~3pp and per anchor only for 10-20pp, so the observed per-anchor gains (Philosophy +16.7, Business +9.1, Chemistry +6.0, against Economics -6.2) were never individually testable; leaf-level rubrics were tested ONCE (+1.8pp, p 0.0498) and the clean follow-up was cancelled by a gate, so that conclusion was weaker than the rest of the line (settled by LEAF-POWERED).

plain_description.what: Using no new calls, the test re-read earlier rubric experiments. It checked whether a rubric makes the judge abstain on the undecidable pairs those tests had discarded. It also checked whether pooling across subjects hid real effects in individual subjects.
plain_description.why: Earlier tests found little value in rubrics, and the question was whether that verdict was an artefact of how they were analysed.
plain_description.information: It tells whether the negative rubric result can be trusted or needs a cleaner test. Result: done. The first explanation was refuted: with or without the rubric, the judge still invents a winner on about 60% of undecidable pairs and still prefers longer answers. The second stayed open: each subject had too few pairs to test effects of the size observed, so per-subject effects could not be tested one by one. This led to LEAF-POWERED, which settled it. Later ruled history rather than evidence, because it ran on the older question pool.
